questions.q: What level does a Security Group filter traffic at, compared to a Network ACL?
options: A Security Group filters at the instance (network interface) level; a Network ACL filters at the subnet level
Both filter at the subnet level, with no difference
A Security Group filters at the subnet level; a Network ACL filters per instance
Security Groups and NACLs both operate only at the VPC level
questions.explain: A Security Group attaches to an instance's network interface; a Network ACL attaches to a subnet and applies to everything in it.

questions.q: What does it mean that a Security Group is "stateful"?
options: If inbound traffic is allowed, the matching outbound response traffic is automatically allowed without a separate rule
It remembers the last 100 connections and blocks repeats
It requires an explicit rule for both inbound and outbound traffic in every case
It only applies to TCP traffic, never UDP
questions.explain: Statefulness means return traffic for an already-allowed connection is automatically permitted, with no matching outbound rule required.

questions.q: Why does a Network ACL rule set often need an outbound rule allowing ports 1024-65535?
options: Because a NACL is stateless, so the ephemeral ports used for return traffic must be explicitly allowed outbound
Because all AWS services communicate exclusively on those ports
Because Security Groups require it, not NACLs
Because those ports are reserved for AWS's own internal traffic
questions.explain: A stateless NACL needs rules in both directions for the same conversation, so the high ephemeral port range must be explicitly allowed outbound.

questions.q: How does AWS evaluate rules in a Network ACL?
options: In ascending order by rule number, stopping at the first rule that matches (allow or deny)
In the order they were created, regardless of rule number
All rules at once, and the most restrictive one always wins
Randomly, to prevent predictable firewall bypass
questions.explain: NACL rules are numbered and evaluated lowest-number first; the first match wins and stops further evaluation.

questions.q: What is the default behavior of a NACL that AWS automatically attaches to a new VPC, versus a custom NACL you create yourself?
options: The default NACL allows all traffic both directions; a custom NACL denies all traffic until rules are added
Both the default and a custom NACL deny all traffic until configured
Both the default and a custom NACL allow all traffic by default
The default NACL only allows outbound traffic, never inbound
questions.explain: The VPC's default NACL starts fully open in both directions, while any custom NACL you create starts fully closed until you add allow rules.
